question: A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient VZV" -> "Acyclovir requires thymidine kinase" -> "Acyclovir ineffective" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient VZV" -> "Famciclovir requires thymidine kinase" -> "Famciclovir ineffective" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient VZV" -> "Ganciclovir requires thymidine kinase" -> "Ganciclovir ineffective" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient VZV" -> "Cidofovir does not require thymidine kinase" -> "Cidofovir effective" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient VZV" -> "Amantadine targets influenza" -> "Amantadine ineffective for VZV" -> 5%
analysis: A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain is resistant to antiviral drugs that require phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase for activation, such as acyclovir, famciclovir, and ganciclovir. Cidofovir, however, does not require activation by viral thymidine kinase and can be effective against such resistant strains. Amantadine is not effective against varicella-zoster virus as it is used for influenza A. Therefore, cidofovir is the best choice for treating this population.
